headline: County clerks expect near-record Missouri turnout
summary: Secretary of State Denny Hoskins projects about 55% turnout, or roughly 2.42 million ballots, just under the 2018 midterm record of 2,442,306. Clerks in Boone and Greene counties expect 57% to 59%, and St. Louis County logged 173,484 early ballots.

headline: $55 million poured into Missouri ballot measures
summary: Spending on the three controversial statewide questions reached $55 million through Friday, with almost $17 million on broadcast ads. The state auditor race is the only statewide candidate contest, so the measures are driving interest.

headline: Missouri ballot: four amendments, Prop A and Boone jail tax
summary: Voters decide Amendments 3, 6, 7 and 8 and Proposition A, the Republican-friendly congressional map, plus Boone County's Proposition L jail sales tax. Polls are open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. and a photo ID is required, with provisional ballots for those without one.

headline: Vance says Stevens endorsement will help Rogers in Michigan
summary: Vice President JD Vance said Rep. Haley Stevens' endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers will help him. Stevens lost the Democratic primary to Abdul El-Sayed.

headline: Governors on the ballot: Florida and Ohio draw national eyes
summary: In Florida, Trump-backed Byron Donalds faces former Republican congressman David Jolly, now a Democrat. In Ohio, Trump-backed Vivek Ramaswamy faces Democrat Amy Acton.

headline: Midterms on pace to be the most expensive on record
summary: OpenSecrets projects about $12 billion in federal spending this cycle, and AdImpact calls it the costliest it has tracked. Wesleyan Media Project puts House, Senate and governor ad spending near $7.1 billion.

headline: Hinson pledges to accept Iowa result, says she will win
summary: Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson said Trump's Dubuque visit helped her portray Democrat Josh Turek as too liberal for Iowa. She said she is confident of victory and will accept the outcome.

headline: Senate stands 53-47 with 11 races deciding control
summary: CBS counts eight Republican-held seats in play, including Alaska, Iowa, Maine, North Carolina and Texas, and three Democratic-held ones in Georgia, Michigan and New Hampshire. In Maine, Sen. Susan Collins faces Democrat Troy Jackson.

headline: CBS picks 47 battleground districts to decide the House
summary: Republicans hold a razor-thin majority, and CBS's Battleground Tracker projects Democrats winning 229 seats. The 47 competitive districts are expected to settle control.

headline: Texas Democrats court Hispanic voters; Abbott race may tighten
summary: Democrats hope to win back Hispanic voters who moved toward Trump in 2024. Gov. Greg Abbott's reelection bid against Gina Hinojosa could also be competitive.

headline: Reuters/Ipsos: 48% call their vote a vote against Trump
summary: Cost of living was the top issue for 48% of registered voters, ahead of democratic norms at 26%. Another 25% said their vote was for Trump, and 55% said military action against Iran was not worth the cost.

headline: Markets give Democrats 95% for House, 76% for Senate
summary: Kalshi and Polymarket had about $1.48 billion wagered on the midterms. Aggregated Monday prices implied a 95% chance of a Democratic House and 76% for the Senate.

headline: DOJ deploys 1,000 monitors; six more charged in California
summary: The Justice Department is sending about 1,000 election monitors to all 50 states, which critics call federal overreach. It also charged six more people in California with alleged voter fraud.

headline: North Carolina early vote runs 35.6% above 2022
summary: North Carolina polls are open 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. Early in-person turnout was 35.6% higher than in 2022 while absentee ballots fell 35%, and registered Democrats led turnout, followed by unaffiliated voters and Republicans.

headline: Five things to watch in Paxton-Talarico Senate race
summary: Polls show the race within the margin of error, with Libertarian Ted Brown at 1% to 3% and possibly keeping the winner under 50%. Key tests are Hispanic voters in South Texas, Tarrant, Collin and Denton counties, Harris County turnout and rural GOP margins.

headline: Justice Department appeals dismissal of Alaska certification suit
summary: After a federal judge in Alaska dismissed the administration's suit aimed at blocking Senate certification if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses, the Justice Department filed a notice of appeal. CBS also reports more than 54 million early votes cast nationally.

headline: Supreme Court refuses to make California set aside 20,000 ballots
summary: The justices rejected the Justice Department's last-minute request to stop California from counting more than 20,000 mail ballots from suspected non-citizens. A lower-court hearing is set for Nov. 13 and certification is due Dec. 3.

headline: Maryland guide: Moore faces Cox as polls open 7 a.m.-8 p.m.
summary: Gov. Wes Moore and Lt. Gov. Aruna Miller face Republicans Dan Cox and Rob Krop. All eight U.S. House seats and all 47 state Senate and 141 House of Delegates seats are also on the ballot, and same-day registration is available.

headline: Final day of early voting across Kansas City metro
summary: Missouri early voting sites in the Kansas City area closed at 5 p.m. Monday, and Kansas sites in Johnson and Wyandotte counties closed at noon. Anyone who missed the window must vote at an assigned precinct Tuesday, when Missouri polls close at 7 p.m.

headline: What's on the Cooper and Howard County ballot
summary: Voters in the area see the 3rd District race (Onder, Mann, Higgins), the 4th District race (Alford, Herrera, Holbrook), a state auditor contest, Missouri House seats 48 and 58, judicial retention votes, and Prop A plus Amendments 3, 6, 7 and 8.

headline: Missouri's secretary of state projects 55% turnout
summary: Secretary of State Denny Hoskins expects about 55% of registered voters to cast ballots, up from roughly 48% in 2022, with Amendments 3, 6, 7 and 8 and Prop A expected to boost turnout. Polls are open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m., and a regular ballot requires an unexpired photo ID.

headline: Iowa Senate finishes as a coin flip between Turek and Hinson
summary: The final-week polling average is Josh Turek 46.0% to Ashley Hinson 45.6%, inside the margin of error. Trump campaigned for Hinson in Sioux City on Nov. 1, while Turek ended his statewide tour in his hometown of Council Bluffs.

headline: Michigan Senate race gets presidential-level star power at the finish
summary: Obama and Sanders campaigned for Abdul El-Sayed while Trump rallied for Mike Rogers, and the RealClearPolitics average has El-Sayed ahead by more than five points. The live blog also reports a Springsteen endorsement of El-Sayed and a $2.4 million fundraising day on Nov. 1.

headline: Wisconsin governor candidates pack 11 events into the last day
summary: Democrat David Crowley rallied in southeast Wisconsin with Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, while Republican Tom Tiffany campaigned with Sen. Ron Johnson and former Gov. Tommy Thompson over the weekend. Both say turnout will decide it; polls close at 8 p.m.

headline: Kansas picks a successor to Gov. Laura Kelly
summary: Republican Ty Masterson faces Democrat Cindy Holscher for governor, alongside the Marshall–Hamilton Senate race. Kansas voters also decide a constitutional amendment on whether only U.S. citizens may vote.

headline: Missouri polls open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. Tuesday; photo ID required
summary: Missouri's ballot includes Amendments 3, 6, 7 and 8, Proposition A on the congressional map, the state auditor race and a Supreme Court judge retention vote, with U.S. House races on the 2022 maps. Voters without an acceptable ID can cast a provisional ballot, and anyone in line at closing can still vote.

headline: Don't expect all 50 states to finish by Wednesday
summary: Experts say some states could take days or weeks, with Maine, Alaska, Arizona and California the slow ones. The House is more likely to be called early because the key Senate races, including Alaska and Maine, are so close.

headline: Maine Senate race could go to a ranked-choice count that takes days
summary: Susan Collins faces Democrat Troy Jackson in what polls describe as a dead heat. Six write-in candidates could keep either under 50%, and Secretary of State Shenna Bellows calls a ranked-choice tabulation highly possible, with results typically final by Nov. 13.

headline: Harvard model: 79% chance Democrats win the Senate, 96% the House
summary: On the eve of the vote, Harvard's model projects about 241 Democratic House seats. Cook expects Democratic House gains of 12 to 25 seats and calls Democrats slight Senate favorites, while Fox News still rates the Senate a toss-up.

headline: Generic ballot at D+8.9; Kalshi gives Democrats 94% for the House
summary: The Silver Bulletin average has Democrats at 51.5% and Republicans at 42.6%, up from D+6.7 on Sept. 1. Kalshi puts Democratic House odds at 93.9%, and ForbesPredict has 83%.

headline: Final polls put Democrats ahead in all seven key Senate states
summary: Forbes' roundup lists Democrats ahead in Michigan (El-Sayed 53–42), Kansas (49–44), Texas (50–43), Maine (51–45), Ohio (49–44), Alaska (48–46) and Iowa (48–47). Only Michigan, Kansas and Texas are tied by name to the Times/Siena poll; the Alaska and Iowa gaps are within the margin of error.

headline: CBS tracker projects Democrats at 229 House seats
summary: CBS's Oct. 25 Battleground Tracker puts Democrats at 229 seats, within a range of 215 to 237, across 47 battleground districts. Republicans hold 218 seats now.

headline: Trump ends campaign swing in Kansas for Marshall
summary: At what he called his 30th and final rally, Trump backed Sen. Roger Marshall against Democrat Adam Hamilton in Salina on Sunday. He had earlier rallied in Dubuque, Iowa.

headline: Judge tosses DOJ suit aimed at Alaska Senate certification
summary: Judge Sharon Gleason dismissed the Justice Department's suit seeking to block certification of Alaska's Senate result unless Sen. Dan Sullivan wins, ruling DOJ lacked standing. DOJ has filed a notice of appeal.

headline: Stevens endorses Rogers over fellow Democrat El-Sayed
summary: Rep. Haley Stevens, who lost Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, endorsed Republican Mike Rogers on Sunday. Schumer and Pelosi sharply criticized her, while El-Sayed's campaign says it raised over $1.2 million afterward.

headline: Trump's final rallies carry a note of nostalgia
summary: He held more than 25 rallies in October, pushing tax cuts, tariffs and border policy, and the RNC reversed a plan to cancel weekend Kansas and Iowa stops. He also floated a $5,000 "Trump dividend" if Republicans win both chambers.

headline: Early vote passes 53 million, far above 2022
summary: A University of Florida analysis counts about 53 million early ballots, versus roughly 46 million in all of 2022's early voting. More than 11 million were cast by registered Democrats and about 8 million by Republicans, though early turnout does not show candidate choice.

headline: Florida Election Day: 7 a.m.–7 p.m., photo ID with signature
summary: Voters must use their assigned precinct, and anyone in line at 7 p.m. can vote. Panhandle counties on Central Time close at 8 p.m. Eastern, and provisional ballots can be cured until 5 p.m. Nov. 5.

headline: Texas early vote tops 7.7 million, a midterm record
summary: Preliminary data show over 7.7 million Texans voted early, about 40.5% of registered voters and above the 2018 record. A Rice University analyst said turnout is high but will not reach presidential levels.

headline: Ohio early vote tops 2022 record as candidates fan out
summary: By Saturday morning about 1.49 million Ohioans had voted early, passing the 2022 midterm total, according to AP figures cited by Fox. Trump held tele-rallies Saturday and planned in-person events in Iowa and Kansas on Sunday.

headline: Early vote tops 43 million as Democrats lead generic polls
summary: An AP analysis cited by Al Jazeera finds over 43 million ballots cast early, about 10 million more than at this point in 2022. RealClearPolling's national average has Democrats ahead by about 8 points.

headline: AP: what to expect in Arizona on Election Day
summary: Gov. Katie Hobbs faces Trump-endorsed Rep. Andy Biggs, and open House seats in the 1st and 6th districts are in play. Polls close at 9 p.m. ET, no results come before 10 p.m. ET, and recounts are automatic at a margin of 0.5% or less.

headline: Georgia early voting ends with record midterm turnout
summary: Nearly 2.3 million early votes were in by Oct. 29, topping the 2022 midterm record for early in-person voting. Trump, Vance, Obama and Harris all made closing appearances in the state.

headline: Paxton drops planned Alamo stop that rules would bar
summary: Paxton canceled a Nov. 2 bus-tour finale at the Alamo, where political events are not permitted on the grounds. He also canceled stops in Texarkana, El Paso and Tyler, and has not explained the Alamo change.

headline: Talarico says Paxton is canceling rallies; camp cites logistics
summary: Democrat James Talarico claimed Ken Paxton is canceling events because few attend, while Paxton's team blamed scheduling for postponing an El Paso rally. Five of six recent polls show Talarico narrowly ahead and Fox has it tied at 49.

headline: Cook moves 14 more races toward Democrats
summary: Cook Political Report shifted two Senate (Florida, Nebraska) and 12 House races, after four governor shifts a day earlier. Cook projects Democrats netting 2 to 6 Senate seats and flipping 12 to 25 House seats.

headline: Judge limits DOJ pressure on California election officials
summary: U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson ordered the administration to stop pressuring election officials over ballots it says belong to ineligible voters, in effect until Nov. 16. The order followed DOJ letters to 57 of California's 58 counties.

headline: Appeals court refuses to set aside 20,000 California ballots
summary: The 9th Circuit ruled 2-1 against a Justice Department request that California set aside ballots tied to about 20,000 people it says may be noncitizens. The panel agreed there is no feasible way to identify those ballots without risking harm to the whole system.

headline: Texas Southern poll: Talarico 49%, Paxton 47%
summary: A survey of 2,000 likely voters taken Oct. 21-25 by Texas Southern University found Democrat James Talarico narrowly ahead of Republican Ken Paxton, with a margin of error of 2.19 points. Talarico also had higher favorability, 48% to 42%.

headline: Stevens' fiance to vote Rogers over El-Sayed remarks
summary: Rep. Haley Stevens said her fiance and her former campaign chair plan to vote for Republican Mike Rogers, citing El-Sayed's rhetoric. Stevens told CNN she still wants El-Sayed to win.

headline: Missouri will use 2022 map; court fights possible after vote
summary: Missouri's general election will use the 2022 congressional map, while voters decide Proposition A on the newer map. Some Republican candidates argue primary voters were disenfranchised, and a close race could bring new lawsuits.

headline: Alaska governor orders probe of Peltola campaign
summary: Gov. Mike Dunleavy ordered an investigation into whether Mary Peltola's Senate campaign helped recruit a second candidate named Dan Sullivan. Peltola called the reporting a distraction from the issues in the race.

headline: CNN polls: Democrats ahead in Texas and Michigan, close in Maine and Kansas
summary: New CNN polls of likely voters show Talarico leading Paxton 49%-43% in Texas and El-Sayed ahead of Rogers 49%-42% in Michigan. Jackson leads Collins 49%-45% in Maine and Hamilton leads Marshall 49%-45% in Kansas, both within the margin of error.

headline: Fox Power Rankings: South Carolina to toss-up, Ohio leans D
summary: Fox News moved South Carolina's Senate race to toss-up and shifted the Ohio Senate and governor races to Lean Democrat. It also moved 19 House races toward Democrats and projects them winning at least 223 seats, with Senate control still unresolved.

headline: Jackson County early voters turn out for amendments and Prop A
summary: Steady lines formed at a Lee's Summit early-voting site as Missouri's statewide questions drive turnout. They include the amendment to repeal the 2024 abortion-rights vote and Proposition A on mid-decade redistricting.

headline: Prop A map vote won't affect this year's House races
summary: Missouri voters decide Proposition A on the 2025 Republican-drawn congressional map, which would apply starting in 2028; the 2022 map is used this year. The opposition campaign has reported $5.4 million in large contributions while the organized GOP effort has gone quiet.

headline: Over 35 million early votes counted before Election Day
summary: About 35.4 million ballots had been cast by roughly Oct. 28, including 16.8 million by mail and 18.5 million in person. Citing NBC News data, Democrats made up 47% of counted votes and Republicans 35%.

headline: No organized campaign backs Prop A map
summary: Prop A opponents have reported $5.4 million in large contributions since mid-September, while the main pro-map group says there is no organized effort to pass it. A yes vote keeps the 2025 congressional map for 2028 and later.

headline: Missouri clergy split over Amendment 3
summary: The state's Catholic bishops and the Missouri Baptist Convention back Amendment 3, which would repeal the 2024 abortion-rights amendment. About 90 clergy members signed a letter opposing it.

headline: Murkowski endorses Democrat for Alaska governor
summary: Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski endorsed Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins in Alaska's race for governor.
